page: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g-240s is a general-purpose instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute series, provisioned on the x86_64 AMD EPYC platform. It delivers 4 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores clocked at 2.0 GHz with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem features 32 MB of shared L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1 data cache per core. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction extensions encompass AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16), AVX-VNNI, SHA-NI, and dedicated AES encryption capabilities. The instance comes bundled with 240 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, and operates without discrete GPU acceleration.

Performance testing reveals distinctive profiles between single-threaded and parallel workloads. Single-core processing demonstrates high efficacy, highlighted by top-tier classifications in stress-ng single-core execution, gzip compression at 39.73 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression at 17.58 GB/sec. Geekbench text processing also registers strong results. In contrast, multi-threaded operations reflect the constraints of its physical dual-core design, yielding lower relative percentiles in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (35.17 GB/sec), multi-core Geekbench scoring (4258.0), and Clang software compilation. Memory subsystem throughput remains balanced across evaluations, reaching 70.96 GB/sec in large uncached reads and 41.27 GB/sec in write operations.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the provision of dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs paired with integrated NVMe storage eliminates the latency overhead of network-attached block devices. The instance maintains dependable performance for I/O and memory-centric operations, evidenced by 8.1 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 14.81 GB/sec static web throughput. For lightweight machine learning workloads, small 135M parameter models process at 664.72 prompt tokens per second, though larger models scale poorly due to the lack of dedicated accelerators. The configuration is primarily matched for web servers, container nodes, backend API layers, relational or key-value datastores, and build pipelines.
description: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g-240s is a general-purpose cloud compute instance configured with 4 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs running on an AMD EPYC processor at 2.0 GHz across 2 physical cores, coupled with 16 GB of system RAM. Hardware acceleration includes AVX-512 vector extensions and SHA and AES cryptographic instructions. The configuration bundles a 240 GB local NVMe SSD and provides one complimentary public IPv4 address, operating without a discrete GPU. In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits strong single-core throughput, ranking in the top tier for single-core stress-ng tests as well as single-threaded compression and decompression routines. However, parallel throughput metrics, such as Geekbench multi-core and multi-threaded compilation, show moderate scaling due to its 2-core hardware topology. The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio and bundled NVMe drive offer balanced compute-to-memory density, making it well matched for web serving, microservices, mid-tier relational databases, in-memory caches, and continuous integration runners.
